cases.title: Installed update restores the existing QA session
preconditions: Task-owned simulator with an existing local QA session
steps: Install current simulator app preserving its data
assertions: Workspace shows Mobile QA greeting and previous test documents

cases.title: Spreadsheet formula survives reopening
preconditions: Isolated QA account and interactive simulator
assertions: B1 shows 200 before and after reopen

cases.title: Presentation edit and slideshow
preconditions: Isolated QA account and interactive simulator
assertions: Title appears in slideshow and after reopening

cases.title: Cache cleanup preserves an offline draft
steps: Clear synced bodies in account settings

lastRun.device: Zhuole Docs QA / iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.1
lastRun.build: Mixed evidence: 7bf19ba baseline; presentation repair; offline/cache on ce151b7; spreadsheet retest on a443485
lastRun.authSource: Task-owned local QA accounts; no credentials logged

results.notes: simctl install and launch succeeded; native screenshot shows restored workspace and previous QA documents.

Browser mirror touch and individual key events entered a numeric 120 and 80 (A2 stored as 080); SUM showed 200 before and after reopening. Read-only local server database query retained =sum(a1:a2), revision 7. The named QA sheet remains for inspection. Retested the a443485 simulator build with a separate local QA account: native input stored A1=120, A2=80, B1 containing =SUM(A1:A2); reopening displayed 200 and independent authenticated API readback matched all three cells. System clipboard acceptance is not established; mirror input/paste forwarding was unreliable.

Initial build placed the close control under the status bar and tapping failed. After native safe-area CSS repair and simulator rebuild/install, the saved title survived reopening, appeared in slideshow, and the visible close button returned to the editor. Local server readback retained the same title at revision 3.

On ce151b7, a loopback proxy disconnected only this app service. Cleared synchronized caches while Word draft was pending, terminated and relaunched the native process offline. The sheet displayed a network-required toast; Word retained Offline draft survives. Reconnection synchronized Word; reopening downloaded the blank sheet. Independent read-only SQLite checks confirmed both originals unchanged before reconnection and the sheet unchanged at revision 1 afterwards. Test fixtures remain for inspection.
